collected_dynamic_variables.pain_frame: We miss calls when we're out on jobs.
collected_dynamic_variables.pain_points: missed calls going to voicemail when out on jobs/after-hours, 50% of callers would book if someone answered, callers want to book an estimate/consultation

transcript:
User: Hello — I got your flyer about after-hours calls. We miss calls when we're out on jobs.
Agent: Got it — when those after-hours calls come in while you’re out on jobs, what usually happens to the caller when nobody picks up?
User: The calls usually go to voicemail if nobody is available to pick up.
Agent: Makes sense — roughly how many calls a week end up going to voicemail like that?
User: About 8 calls a week end up going to voicemail.
Agent: Got it — when those 8 calls hit voicemail, do most people leave a message, or do they usually just move on?
User: Most people leave a message, but about 50% would book if someone answered.
Agent: Yeah, that’s a lot of bookings getting delayed or lost — what kind of business are you in?
User: I run a home remodeling and contractor company in Denver.
Agent: Got it — in your Denver remodeling business, when someone calls after-hours, what’s the #1 thing they usually want right then (a ballpark quote, to book an estimate, or something else)?
User: They usually want to book an estimate or consultation for a remodeling project.
Agent: Got it — mind if I do a quick 30‑second calculation on what those missed estimate calls might be costing you?
User: Sure, go ahead.
Agent: Perfect — what’s your average ticket value for a remodeling job that comes from one of those booked estimates (ballpark)?
User: The average job value is about $2,500.
Agent: Got it — if you booked even 50% of those 8 missed calls, that’s about **$10,000 extra a week**… and that’s just one week—about **$43,300 a month**. Does that feel about right?
User: Yes, that sounds about right, considering the average job value and the number of missed calls.
Agent: Mhm, makes sense — it adds up fast. It’s a 20-minute walkthrough where Jay will show you exactly how we stop those missed estimate calls from turning into lost jobs; what’s better for you — later today or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow would work better for me.
Agent: Perfect — before I lock a time in for tomorrow, what’s your first name?
User: I prefer not to use names. Let's just proceed with booking the live call for tomorrow.
Agent: Got it — to book it, I do need a first and last name for the calendar invite. What first name should I put down?
User: Just use 'Cornerstone Remodeling' for the calendar invite, please.
Agent: Got it — I can use Cornerstone Remodeling as the company name, but I still need a first and last name on the invite. What name should I put down?
User: Just use 'the live call' or 'the demo' for the invite, please.
Agent: Got it — I still need a first and last name to put the invite under. What first name should I use?
User: Just use 'Cornerstone' or 'the team' instead of my name, please.
Agent: Got it — I can put “Cornerstone” on the invite, but I still need a real first and last name to finalize the booking. What first name should I use?
User: Just put 'Cornerstone Team' on the invite; we prefer to keep it under the company name.
Agent: Got it — I can put “Cornerstone Team” as the name on the invite. What’s the best contact number to send the SMS confirmation to?
User: The best contact number is +13039150001 for SMS confirmation.
Agent: Got it — and which time zone are you in: Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
User: I'm in the Mountain timezone, which is America/Denver.
Agent: Got it — and what last name should I put down for the invite?
User: Just use 'Cornerstone Remodeling'; we prefer to keep it under the company name.
Agent: Got it — quick check: the number to text is **+1 (303) 915-0001**, and you’re on **Mountain time**, right?
User: Yes, that's correct. Please text +13039150001, and we are indeed on Mountain time.
Agent: Perfect — I can get you in tomorrow as soon as **10:30 AM** or **11:15 AM** Mountain time. Which works?
User: 10:30 AM Mountain time works for me. Please book it.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: My calendar is giving me trouble at 10:30—let me try the next closest slot.
Agent: My calendar is giving me trouble right now—let me re-run it once more to make sure everything sticks.
Agent: We’re having trouble confirming the calendar — we’ll reach you at your number within the hour to lock in the time. Thanks for calling, and we’ll talk soon.
